one_liner: Cython/libuv replacement for CPython's default asyncio event loop; 2-4x echo throughput in its own 2016 benchmark.
what_it_does: uvloop is a full implementation of asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, written in Cython on top of a vendored libuv (the Node.js I/O library). asyncio code (Tasks, streams, protocols) and libraries such as uvicorn or aiohttp run on it unchanged. You opt in per program with uvloop.run(main()) (0.18+) or asyncio.run/asyncio.Runner(loop_factory=uvloop.new_event_loop). The older uvloop.install() warns from Python 3.12, and both install() and EventLoopPolicy are removed for 3.16. It uses the same API as the stdlib loop rather than a new framework, but a few loop methods are missing (see when_not_to_use).
how_it_is_fast: The loop's hot paths are compiled C instead of interpreted Python. A Cython loop drains the ready deque, Handle/TimerHandle objects come from 250-entry Cython freelists, and uv_run() runs with the GIL released while libuv waits in epoll/kqueue. Transport.write first tries a direct write() syscall for one buffer, or uv_try_write (scatter-gather) for several, and queues a uv_write only when the socket would block. Reads go into one preallocated 256,000-byte buffer per loop. TLS is a Cython port of asyncio's SSLProtocol over Python's ssl module, not libuv. The kernel side is the same readiness-based epoll/kqueue as the stdlib selector loop, so the gain comes from less per-event interpreter overhead, not a different I/O interface.
when_to_use: Long-running asyncio network services on Linux or macOS (uvicorn/ASGI apps, aiohttp, websockets, custom asyncio.Protocol servers) where profiles show time in the event loop itself.

Many small messages or many callbacks/task switches: the 2016 chart shows the biggest gaps at 1 KiB (about 2.5x for the protocol API, 3.9x for sock_recv/sock_sendall), and a 2026 CPython 3.14.7 run still found 2.15x on 200k callbacks and 1.6x on 50k tasks.
Worker-thread hand-off via call_soon_threadsafe: a third-party benchmark (python-async-bench, Python version and hardware not stated) measured 3.47 s vs 5.88 s wall time for 250k messages.

You want a speedup from a one-line change with no rewrite, and your deployment can use the prebuilt wheels: CPython 3.8-3.14 including free-threaded 3.14t, manylinux/musllinux x86-64/aarch64, macOS x86-64/universal2.
when_not_to_use: Windows: setup.py refuses to build there ('uvloop does not support Windows at the moment'), and the request has been open since 2016 (#14). There you must use asyncio's own loops.

Code that needs loop.sendfile/sock_sendfile (open since 2019, #228), sock_recvfrom/sock_recvfrom_into/sock_sendto (these raise NotImplementedError), Server.close_clients from 3.13 (#683), or create_connection's happy_eyeballs_delay/interleave (not in the signature, #406).

Large-message, bulk or TLS-bound traffic, or apps whose own code dominates. At 100 KiB the first-party gap drops to about 1.4x (streams) and 1.8x (protocol). A 2026 Linux run on CPython 3.14.7 measured only 1.19x over stdlib asyncio for 1 KiB streams round trips. The 2016 blog itself found aiohttp's HTTP parser, not the loop, was the bottleneck.
PyPy, GraalPy or other non-CPython runtimes: the package declares CPython only, and PyPy install/import failures are open issues (#380, #537).

Deployments that need recent fixes from PyPI: 0.22.1 (2025-10-16) is still the latest release. The free-threading call_soon_threadsafe race fix (#720), eager_start support and the 2026 write-path/SSL speedups exist only on master. A segfault in __uv_close_handle_cb under uvicorn/FastAPI is still open (#706).

integration.dependencies: none at runtime: libuv is vendored and built into the wheel. Source builds need Cython ~=3.1, setuptools>=60, packaging and a C compiler, plus autotools when building libuv from a git checkout. The --use-system-libuv option links against a system libuv instead.
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.8.1+ (wheels cp38-cp314 plus cp314t). A source build needs Cython ~=3.1 and a C compiler; it uses -O2 by default (override with UVLOOP_OPT_CFLAGS).
integration.platforms: Linux (manylinux2014 and musllinux_1_2, x86-64 and aarch64) and macOS (x86-64, universal2). No Windows. CPython only.
integration.thread_safety: One loop per thread, as in asyncio. Only call_soon_threadsafe is safe to call from other threads, and wrong-thread calls are detected only in debug mode. Free-threaded 3.14t wheels ship, but a call_soon_threadsafe race under free-threading (#720) is fixed only on unreleased master.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same asyncio.AbstractEventLoop API, selected with uvloop.run() or loop_factory, and most asyncio code runs unchanged. Missing: Windows support, sendfile/sock_sendfile, sock_recvfrom/sock_recvfrom_into/sock_sendto, Server.close_clients, and happy-eyeballs arguments. subprocess_exec rejects startupinfo/creationflags and requires bufsize=0.

gotchas: Selecting the loop: uvloop.install() emits DeprecationWarning on 3.12+, and install() and EventLoopPolicy are removed for 3.16. The policy's get_event_loop() raises RuntimeError when no loop is set, where older stdlib policies created one (#702, open). Some libraries broke on this.
Debug mode (PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1 or debug=True) can crash during async-generator finalization on Python 3.13/3.14 (#715, open; one report says aarch64 only). Keep debug mode out of production.

Behavior differs from stdlib in edge cases. libuv's process spawn can briefly block the loop (#118, open since 2017), and one user reported responses being coalesced under uvicorn but not under stdlib asyncio (#631, open).
Memory is not necessarily lower: an HN user measured 204 MB vs 171 MB max RSS for 100k sleeping tasks under uvloop vs asyncio on an M1 Mac (anecdotal, CPython 3.12+).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick uvloop when you are staying in Python asyncio: it is the only catalogued entry that speeds up existing asyncio code without changing it. UCall beats FastAPI/uvicorn only by replacing the whole server stack with its own JSON-RPC server. libhv, libev and picoev are C event libraries (libhv even benchmarks ahead of libuv, which uvloop wraps) that help only if you leave Python.
verified_claims_summary: MagicStack's own 2016 vmbench echo servers ran single-threaded in Docker (concurrency 10, 30 s runs, TCP_NODELAY) on a Xeon E5-1620 v2, Ubuntu, Python 3.5; compiler and flags are not given. Against the stdlib selector loop, uvloop measured about 2.5x (protocol API), 3.9x (sock_recv/sock_sendall) and 2.5x (streams) at 1 KiB, and about 1.4-1.8x at 100 KiB. A 2026 third-party run (rsloop's benchmark doc: i9-9900K, Linux, CPython 3.14.7, uvloop 0.22.1) still put uvloop ahead of stdlib asyncio, by less: 2.15x on callbacks, 1.62x on tasks and 1.19x on 1 KiB TCP streams round trips.
status_note: Actively maintained (commits through 2026-07-14, CI on CPython 3.8-3.14t) but releases lag: 0.22.1 from 2025-10-16 is still the latest on PyPI. Dual Apache-2.0/MIT, installed as prebuilt wheels with no runtime dependencies.
